reviewed.new-york-control/bottom|New York Control: SEAT INVERSION in the POSITION file, not a trap and NOT a name collision (corrected v1.141.2 -- the earlier note here asserted two techniques share the name; a panel disproved it). There is ONE referent: Eddie Bravo's no-gi rubber-guard choke. The proof is the one field an LLM pass may not write -- `content/Positions/Rubber Guard/Invisible Collar.json` carries eight machine-verified clips and six name the position outright ('Invisible Collar (MTS 134)' -- Eddie Bravo; 'Invisible Collar choke from Rubber Guard'; 'Double Invisible Collar cross choke, no-gi' -- Denny Prokopos), with THREE of them filed on the `top` role whose own prerequisites demand 'Opponent wearing gi'. Zero gi back-control footage anywhere on the file. The prose was a confabulated gi back-mount at its birth commit (0734e5cf7), complete with a fabricated Eddie Bravo quote explaining the contradiction away. The directory says it too: the file lives under `Rubber Guard/`. So the two New York transitions are CORRECT and must not be re-pointed; the defect is that the position's two hands are swapped -- bottom holds escapes and top holds the finishes, when the rubber-guard player attacks from the BOTTOM. Measured counterfactual: swapping only `position_type` + `strength` leaves this audit byte-identical; swapping the HANDS clears both rows. So this is content re-authoring, not a two-field flip, and FLOW must not print a backfiring badge for this family until it lands.
reviewed.rear-triangle/top|Kimura from Back: THE PRICE OF THE KIMURA TRAP SEAT RULING (v1.157.0, decided_by owner_decision — the ruling itself is in tests/artifacts/seat_deck_baseline.json `reviewed`, which is the ledger validate_seat_decks.py reads). `Kimura from Kimura Trap` moved from Kimura Trap/Top to Kimura Trap/Bottom, because Bottom is the seat that holds the lock. Kimura Trap/Top therefore no longer has a direct finish, so arriving there is worth less than it was, and every success cell that feeds it drops. That is this baseline's FIRST category — 'a real trap the score should price' — not an authoring defect: succeeding into a state where your own arm is in the opponent's figure four and you cannot finish SHOULD be priced as a trap. Measured, and the least-damaging option of the three tried: Kimura alone gives these 2 rows and V0 0.076847; also moving `Americana from Kimura Trap` gives 5 rows and V0 0.076437; re-homing the six grip-establishing success edges onto Bottom gives 3 rows and V0 0.076542. The owner's literal instruction measured best and is what shipped. WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY CLEAR THESE, and it is a separate content decision: Kimura Trap/Top still deals `North-South to Kimura` and `Kimura to Back Take`, grip-HOLDER moves on a seat that no longer holds the grip. The position conflates a top kimura trap (entered from north-south, back, crab ride) with a bottom one (entered from half guard); splitting it is the real fix and was not ruled on.
